content.text: Section 24 is a full customer-favourable assignment regime, and no other clause (including § 9 termination) creates a change-of-control right. No redline needed.

input.quote:
24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. ... 24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld ... 24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 24 meets the preferred position. § 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or to a merger/acquisition/substantially-all-assets successor without Vendor's consent (notice only); § 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, subject to a reasonableness standard, and restricts assignment to a direct competitor; § 24.3 makes any other assignment consent-based with a not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard; and § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration, or service-reduction right on our change of control. § 13 (p0056) reinforces our right to transfer licence rights on a permitted Section 24 assignment, and § 9 contains only an insolvency trigger, not a change-of-control trigger. The only wording short of preferred is that Vendor's competitor bar reads "direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent" rather than an absolute never — a minor sub-element we note but do not redline, since the gate is our own consent.</rationale>
